speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the consultation. I need to understand your psychiatric condition and this new movement disorder you are experiencing. To start, can you describe the specific movements you are noticing and when they began?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful context. Given your recent diagnosis of schizophrenia and the start of risperidone, could you describe the specific type of movement disorder you are experiencing? For example, are they involuntary muscle contractions, a tremor, or a feeling of restlessness?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The symptoms you describe—specifically the inability to remain still, persistent restlessness, and repetitive pacing—sound like akathisia, a common side effect of risperidone. Have you noticed any worsening of these feelings in the last few days or weeks?
